# Power flattening adds the volume and surface entropy responses

This is a bounded supplement to the SAME-separator regular physical
source. It identifies an exact simultaneous physical/parameter direction;
it does not identify its two martingale couplings. The resulting two
nonnegative deficits have the SAME sign. Consequently this natural power
flattening action is not an entropic cancellation mechanism. No universal
comparison between the separate deficits is proved or presumed.

## 1. Standing regular physical scope

Use precisely the setting and notation of
`candidate 8f0725a173821a00`.
In particular the positive finite-plane concave L is geometrically
normalized on the actual mixed volume m:

    M^(-1) integral log L dm=0.

There is one joint physical/parameter separator eta, regular proper
singleton contact groups (and possibly atomic cover rows), with

    e_i=eta_i delta_i,       Delta=sum_proper e_i>0,
    sigma_i=e_i/Delta,       N=d+1,       kappa=Delta/(NM).

The body improvement density is Xi and its common-separator inequality
is integral_boundary Xi v plus the parameter response <=0. The physical
cone is assumed to contain the actually realizable common signed convex
fields supplied by complete global cuts. In particular it contains the
convex extension of B=-kappa log L. This is an explicit feasibility
premise, not an assumption that unrelated formal velocities add.

The volume martingale is the normalized version of the same-eta one:

    mu=sum_i sigma_i/L_i delta_(Y_i),
    nu=dm/(M L),             L_i=L(Y_i).

Write nu_i for its row from Y_i and m_i=sigma_i/L_i. We omit sigma-zero
rows. The separate surface coupling, when used, is from Xi_+ dS to
Xi_- dS. No equality of these marginals is asserted.

## 2. The exact volume entropy and original-volume row allocations

Set

    rho_i=nu_i/m_i,
    d(bar rho_i)=(L/L_i) d rho_i.

Each is a probability measure because the volume row preserves L.
Moreover

    sum_i sigma_i bar rho_i=dm/M.

The density ratio is bounded above and below by positive constants.
Thus relative entropy is finite, and direct integration gives

    K_V:=sum_i sigma_i KL(bar rho_i || rho_i)
       =M^(-1) integral log L dm-sum_i sigma_i log L_i
       =-sum_i sigma_i log L_i >=0.                     (1)

This identity is independent of which feasible contact martingale rows
are chosen. Its nonnegativity also follows directly by testing the
parameter cone with h=-L log L, as below. The row measures and their
original-volume reweighting are proved in Two-sided's
`candidate 9e43ca1dd488e8cb`;
the elementary derivation here fixes the same-eta normalization needed
for the physical formula.

Equality in (1) holds exactly when EVERY positive row preserves L
pointwise: L(w)=L_i for nu_i-a.e. w. This follows from equality in the
nonnegative relative entropy, not merely equality in concave Jensen.
Jensen equality alone already holds for these rows and is weaker.

## 3. An exact feasible power path, including signed body changes

For 0<=t<1 the raw parameter

    L_t^raw=L^(1-t)                                     (2)

is concave: the power is increasing and concave on positive values, and
L is concave. At fixed bodies it is ALREADY logarithmically normalized,
since <log L_t^raw>=(1-t)<log L>=0. Its derivative is

    h=-L log L,             <h/L>=-<log L>=0.            (3)

This is also an exact radial feasible tangent. Fix a compact common
neighborhood on which L stays positive, and choose C>=1+log of its maximum
on that neighborhood. The function
g(s)=Cs-s log s is increasing and concave there, so
h+C L=g(L) has a concave extension to a common neighborhood of the old
bodies on which the same finite-plane L remains positive. This verifies
the simultaneous body/parameter feasibility requirement from the cited
physical source.

The body field

    v(w)=B(w)=-kappa log L(w)                            (4)

is the restriction of a globally finite convex function: extend each
-kappa log A_r below its positive minimum on a common compact neighborhood
by its tangent line and take the maximum. The signed complete-cut
construction makes this an actual compatible first normal speed.
Positive values give inward motion and negative values outward motion.
The field is NOT required to be a nonnegative erosion.

For the simultaneous actual body path K_t, use the exact normalized
parameter obtained from (2) by dividing by its geometric mean on K_t.
The shape normalization adds the already retained term s(v) L. Thus
the common response formula applies with precisely v from (4) and h
from (3); it does not omit the varying body measure in the normalization.

## 4. The two deficits add in the one common response

Let

    R=-integral_boundary Xi B dS

be the surface logarithmic reserve. Under the physical convex-potential
tests it is nonnegative. When represented by the separate surface
martingale pi_S it equals

    R=kappa integral [log L(w)-log L(w')] d pi_S.        (5)

The exact common-separator response for a raw parameter direction h is

    R_param(h)=-(1/N)sum_i e_i h(Y_i)/L_i
                       +(Delta/N)<h/L>.

Substituting (3) and (1) gives

    R_param(-L log L)=(1/N)sum_i e_i log L_i
                    =-Delta K_V/N.                    (6)

The body response to (4) is exactly -R by its definition. Therefore the
simultaneous legal direction has weighted improvement

    R_joint=-(R+Delta K_V/N)<=0.                        (7)

More generally independently nonnegative multiples of the two allowed
directions give the corresponding nonnegative linear combination of
these two costs. They do not cancel.

Equation (7) is a statement about the SAME-eta weighted COVERING
response. It is not by itself an assertion that the actual maximum
depth increases: selected upper covers need not supply the exact depth
derivative. What it does prove is that this proposed joint entropy
flattening direction is completely consistent with the separating
inequality, even when both deficits are positive. It supplies no
contradiction to a putative minimum.

## 5. Exact conditional zero-response rigidity

If this particular weighted response is zero, then R=K_V=0 separately.
The volume coupling consequently preserves L pointwise on each row.
In the finite-PL setting it also forces every positive source continuous
gradient c_i to vanish. Indeed its row lies on a contacting affine plane
A_i and has positive mass absolutely continuous in the sampled fibers.
If c_i were nonzero, the additional constraint A_i=L_i would cut every
fiber in a d-volume-null hyperplane, impossible. Gradient-label exhaustion
then gives grad_X L=0 almost everywhere in every sampled fiber. Since
each fiber restriction is continuous finite PL and connected, it is
constant on that fiber. It may still vary from one base to another.

For the separate surface coupling, the established quantitative bound

    R>=kappa integral [L(w)-E(L(w')|w)]/L(w) dmu_S
       +kappa/(2L_max^2) integral [L(w')-L(w)]^2 d pi_S

has both terms nonnegative. Thus R=0 forces pointwise preservation of L
on its rows as well. Neither coupling can then fund a different L level.

This is conditional zero-response rigidity only. Body or parameter
stationarity does NOT say that the one-sided power path is neutral,
and it does not set either deficit to zero.

There is an exact reverse-direction obstruction for EVERY nonconstant
finite-PL L, not just for a specially chosen affine example. Some
relative-open full-dimensional cell inside C has a nonconstant active
affine function A. Otherwise the continuous PL function would be constant
on the connected relative interior and then on C. On a short segment
inside that cell where A varies, L^(1+t)=A^(1+t) is strictly convex for
every t>0. Also h_rev=L log L has strictly positive second derivative
along that segment, while any scalar multiple of L is affine there.
Thus h_rev+cL is not concave for ANY c: the reverse direction is not in
the exact radial tangent cone.

It is not even a uniform first-order limit of concave feasible paths on
that segment. The old L has equality in its midpoint Jensen inequality;
dividing the path's nonnegative midpoint concavity gap by t forces the
same concavity inequality for any uniform first derivative. The reverse
h_rev violates it strictly. This remains true under small body changes
that preserve the segment in a common relative-interior ball. Therefore
one cannot obtain the opposite sign in (7) by a hidden two-sided test or
by a merely infinitesimal approximation to the reversed power.

## 6. What has and has not been decided

The actual power path and the convex logarithmic body field provide an
exact bridge at the level of the common response: their entropies add
as in (7). The frequently tempting cancellation is not a valid identity.
No inequality comparing the magnitudes of R and K_V in general is proved.

The independent one-gradient interval calibration proves that volume
transport and global fixed-body parameter optimality alone do not pay
Gamma. It is not a joint body minimum and cannot supply a physical
surface martingale for Xi without checking that extra condition. In
particular a numerical sign of its formal boundary integral must not be
reported as a certified surface entropy. A different compatible
physical direction or additional geometry would be required to turn
the present deficits into a descending response.
